body:
## Observed regression

PR #22's ancestry-aware intake validator blocks the required no-rewrite synchronization path for every pre-law canonical-remediation PR.

Reproduced on PR #19 (`kb/shadows-over-camelot-rules-components`) from exact remote head `2e0b266dec6f296117c4ae70197a820ba2f2204d`:

1. fetched current `origin/main` at `c471bf43f97edfa60aa781a69248e5aa5af4c6ce`;
2. merged `origin/main` into the remediation branch without rebase, force-push, or history rewriting;
3. resolved the sole conflict in deterministic `TELEMETRY.md` by preserving both histories;
4. obtained merge commit `01efceb41ab9eb22f03deaa941691e6f88050137` with parents `2e0b266...` and `c471bf4...`;
5. ran the current required local gate:

```text
node scripts/validate-intake.mjs --base origin/main
```

Result: **19 findings**. Every protected Shadows over Camelot path, plus the merged legacy Unsettled packet paths, reports that parent `e0e47b2f7593f5ee34c25c5695be9b6bed172afd` "falls outside the validated base ancestry."

Using the old common base does not produce a lawful workaround:

```text
node scripts/validate-intake.mjs --base e0e47b2f7593f5ee34c25c5695be9b6bed172afd
```

That causes the already-merged legacy Unsettled blocked packet to be treated as newly introduced and rejected under the new issue-only law. The tracked pre-push hook hardcodes `origin/main`, so the required push cannot pass without bypassing a fail-closed gate. No bypass was attempted; PR #19 was not pushed or merged.

## Impact

- All seven open canonical-remediation PRs (#13–#19) are based on `e0e47b2...`, now conflict with current `main`, and are required by campaign law to merge current `main` without rewriting history before fresh CI/audit.
- The current validator cannot simultaneously grandfather main's already-accepted legacy intake history and validate a pre-law remediation branch's preserved ancestry.
- This makes the mandated remediation synchronization path impossible under the repository's own pre-push gate.

## Required repair

- [ ] Add a disposable-history regression that starts with a legacy canonical-remediation branch and a newer main containing grandfathered blocked intake history.
- [ ] Merge current main into that branch without rewriting history.
- [ ] Require protected-history validation to inspect the branch ancestry without treating legitimate ancestors of the current base as unknown.
- [ ] Continue rejecting mutate/restore, add/delete, rename-out, partial-canonical-before-promotion, and newly committed blocked packets.
- [ ] Make the ordinary pre-push invocation and GitHub synthetic-merge invocation agree on this legacy synchronization case.
- [ ] Obtain a fresh independent exact-head PASS on the workflow repair before merge.

## Closure condition

Close only when the exact legacy-remediation sync fixture passes locally and in PR CI while all PR #22 adversarial history fixtures remain green. Do not weaken or bypass the gate merely to move the old PRs.
title: workflow: legacy canonical-remediation branches cannot sync current main
